nl.statement: A sharp bivariate boundary-discontinuity superpopulation model. A law \(P\) for \((Y(0),Y(1),X)\) with \(X\in\mathbb R^2\) and real potential outcomes is observed through the known Borel assignment regions \(\mathcal A_0,\mathcal A_1\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) with common compact boundary \(\mathcal B=\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_0)\cap\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_1)\): the treatment is the deterministic indicator \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_1\}\), the observed outcome is \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\), and the observed unit is \(O=(Y,X)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\). The sample \(\mathcal D_n=(O_i:1\le i\le n)\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\). For each side \(t\in\{0,1\}\) the one-sided restricted score measure is \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\), with closed support \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{t,P})\); the side regression \(g_{t,P}\) is a Borel representative on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\) of \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]\) taken modulo \(\mu_{t,P}\), its boundary trace is \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)\), and the target estimand is the boundary causal trace contrast \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\) on \(\mathcal B\). Local information is measured by the one-sided local-mass function \(q_{t,P}(x,h)=P\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le h\}\) with \(d(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\), by its two-sided minimum \(a_P(x,h)=\min_{t}q_{t,P}(x,h)\), by the thin-site packing profile \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) — the largest cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\{x\in\mathcal B:a_P(x,h)\le u\}\), declared for all \(u\in[0,\infty)\) — and by the local effective multiplicity \(K_P(x,h)=1\vee\mathsf J_P(h,a_P(x,h))\). Fixed constants are the localization radius \(h_0\in(0,1)\), the Lipschitz and trace envelope \(L>0\), the known sub-Gaussian noise scale \(\sigma>0\), the mass constants \(0<c_m<C_m\), and the exponent range \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\). Law classes are carved out of this world by member conditions: the polynomial-thickness class \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{base}}\), its isolated and pervasive thinning subclasses \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the declared modulus--lower-profile class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_-)\) built from a nondecreasing modulus \(m\) and a lower packing envelope \(\mathsf J_-\), and the triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\) over declared triples \((\kappa,\mathsf J_-,\mathsf J_+)\). — Search trace: `npm run search -- "boundary discontinuity two-sided regression trace"` / `"one-sided restricted score measure support"` / `"local mass ball boundary"` over `Causalean/PO/`, `Causalean/Stat/`, `Causalean/Estimation/`; plus grep of `../doc/API.md` sections 8h (`PO/`), 9i0 (`PO/Analysis/Regression.lean`), 9i0b (`PO/ID/Exact/RDD/RDDLimits.lean`), 9i' (SharpRDD), 12 (`Stat/`), 12w (`Stat/Minimax/`) and of `doc/API.md` section 3.13. Result: Causalean's boundary/RDD substrate (`Causalean.PO.RDDLimits.oneSidedLimit_eq_right/_left`, `POSharpRDDSystem`) is the SCALAR cutoff world on \(\mathbb R\) with a two-sided-support premise at a single point; it does not carry a planar assignment region, a compact boundary curve, a restricted-score support, or a local-mass function, so it cannot bind these symbols. The nearest planar world, `CausalSmith.Stat.BddUniformLogPenalty` (doc/API.md 3.13), is the CTY common-map distance-architecture class with a POSITIVE score density and is a converse-only decision-theoretic world: wrong class, wrong architecture. Bypass-justified: this world is scaffolded over Mathlib + the listed Causalean primitives. Reused inside the block rather than rebuilt: `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample` for the i.i.d. sampling structure, `Causalean.Mathlib.CondDistrib` for the regular conditional outcome kernel \(\mathsf R_P\), `ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF` / `HasCondSubgaussianMGF` for the residual tail, and `Metric.packingNumber` for \(h\)-separated cardinalities behind \(\mathsf J_P\) and the boundary entropy condition. Analogous module for the one-sided-limit step: `Causalean/PO/ID/Exact/RDD/RDDLimits.lean` — F3 should adapt `oneSidedLimit_eq_left/right` from the half-line filter \(\mathcal N[<]c\) to the restricted-support filter \(z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\); the gap to bridge is that positivity of one-sided mass now comes from the polynomial lower-mass member condition rather than from a scalar support premise.

The observable estimation layer over the model of \(\mathrm{S1}\), together with its decision-theoretic risk. Tuning is confined to the dyadic bandwidth grid \(\mathcal H_n=\{2^{-j}h_0:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\}\). From the sample one forms the one-sided counts \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i\le n}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\), the side-specific local-constant fits \(\widehat g_{t,n}(x;h)\), the count-qualified admissible set \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\), the count-adaptive bandwidth \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) with its deterministic tie-break and its \(h_0\) fallback, and the mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\). Performance is measured by the expected-supremum minimax risk \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), the infimum running over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry, and it is compared against the two frontier rates \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\). — Search trace: `npm run search -- "minimax risk supremum over a law class"`, `"local constant regression estimator bandwidth selection"`, `"Lepski bandwidth selection empirical count"` over `Causalean/Stat/Minimax/`, `Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/`, `Causalean/Estimation/`; grep `^## ` on `../doc/API.md` then read of sections 12w (Minimax), 12'.f' (BinomialCount), 10z. Mathlib check via `lean_leansearch` for a supremum-loss minimax value: `ProbabilityTheory.minimaxRisk` (Mathlib `Probability/Decision/Risk/Defs.lean`) is a Bayes/decision-kernel risk over a fixed loss and does NOT type-match an expected-sup-over-a-boundary-curve risk with an estimator ranging over sample-measurable maps into a function space, and `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.MinimaxRisk` carries `sqRisk`/two-point plumbing for a REAL functional, not a sup-norm curve loss. So the risk functional is define-local; `Causalean.Stat.sqRisk`'s file is nonetheless imported because the two-point/Le Cam interface there is what the lower bounds compose with. Genuinely reused rather than rebuilt: `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.clipIcc` (+ `clipIcc_mem_Icc`, `abs_clipIcc_sub_le`, `measurable_clipIcc`, `lipschitzWith_clipIcc`) for the \([-2L,2L]\) projection and the "projection cannot increase the error" step, and `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.bernoulliCount_lower_tail` for the binomial lower tail \(\Pr(N\le nq/2)\le e^{-nq/8}\) that appears as equations (29), (37), (53) and (106) of the core proofs.

The honest-inference layer. For a target simultaneous miscoverage level \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), a band is a data-measurable map \(\mathcal C_n\) sending each boundary location \(x\in\mathcal B\) to an interval in \(\mathbb R\), with half-width \(W_n(x)=\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_n(x))/2\). Honesty over a law class is simultaneous coverage \(P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\ \text{for every}\ x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma\) (or \(\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) for a vanishing slack), and width is judged against the local thickness--entropy benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_n}[2Lh+\sigma\sqrt{n^{-1}\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}(q_{0,P}(x,h)^{-1}+q_{1,P}(x,h)^{-1})}]\). Distinguishability between two full observed laws is measured by the total-variation distance \(\operatorname{TV}(Q,Q')=\sup_E|Q(E)-Q'(E)|\). — Search trace: `npm run search -- "honest confidence band simultaneous coverage width"`, `"total variation coverage transfer"`, `"expected length confidence set lower bound"` over `Causalean/Stat/Minimax/`, `Causalean/Estimation/Inference/`; read of `../doc/API.md` 12w.1 and 12w.11. Genuine reuse: `Causalean.Stat.tvDist` binds the symbol \(\operatorname{TV}\) exactly (`⨆ A measurable, |μ.real A − ν.real A|`), and `Causalean.Stat.abs_measureReal_sub_le_tvDist` is the variational step used at equation (120) of `thm:global-honest-band-and-width-obstruction`. Analogous module for the width converse: `Causalean/Stat/Minimax/HonestConfidenceSet.lean` — `Causalean.Stat.coverage_tv_expectedRestrictedVolume_lower` is the same coverage-to-expected-width argument but for a random SUBSET of \(\mathbb R\) measured by Lebesgue volume over a one-dimensional parameter region; the gap to bridge is that here the loss is the half-width of an interval at a fixed boundary location \(x\in\mathcal B\) and the supremum is over the boundary curve, so the Tonelli volume identity does not apply and the decoding argument of `lem:geometry-general-pervasive-band-width-obstruction` is used instead. Bypass-justified for the band object itself: no Causalean type carries a boundary-curve-indexed interval band.

The explicit witness and diagnostic geometry. Write \(\rho(z)=\lVert z\rVert_2-1\) for the signed distance to the unit circle, \(\mathcal T=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:|\rho(z)|\le h_0\}\) for the symmetric circular tube, and fix a site \(x_\star\in S^1\). On \(\mathcal T\) the two normalized score densities are \(f_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\propto\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}\) and \(f_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\propto\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_\star)/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\); the baseline witness laws \(P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) and \(P_\kappa^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) give \(X\) the corresponding density and set \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\) with independent standard normal \(Z_0,Z_1\), so both have identically vanishing side regressions and traces. Perturbed experiments are indexed by a maximal \(3h\)-separated set \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq S^1\) and the scale-dependent Lipschitz tents \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), with \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\): the laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) keep the score density and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\), \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Two separate geometric diagnostics live here: the polynomial horn \(\mathsf H_\kappa=\{(u,v):0<u<h_0,\ |v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\), and, for a severity exponent \(\alpha>0\), the exponential horn mass modulus \(m_\alpha(h)=\int_0^h2\exp(-u^{-\alpha})\,du\). — Search trace (Causalean): `Grep "halfDisc" ../Causalean` -> only `Causalean/Mathlib/Analysis/HalfDiscPolar.lean`; `Grep -i "annul|tubular|signedDistance|normalCoord" ../Causalean` -> only `Stat/Concentration/Covering/EuclideanRadialPolynomial/{Geometry,Cover,Score}.lean` (`radialAnnulusMonomial`, a VC/pseudo-dimension class of radial monomials supported on a relative annulus — a function class, not a change of variables) and `Stat/PolynomialTail/MomentIBounds.lean`; `Grep "polarCoord|integral_comp_polarCoord|Jacobian" ../Causalean` -> `HalfDiscPolar.lean` is the ONLY integration-side polar file (the other `Jacobian` hits are M-estimation derivative matrices and `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/PolynomialImageDimension/Jacobian.lean`). Search trace (Mathlib): `lean_leansearch "change of variables to polar coordinates for integral over the plane"` -> `integral_comp_polarCoord_symm`, `lintegral_comp_polarCoord_symm` (`Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.PolarCoord`), `MeasureTheory.lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul` (`Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.Jacobian`); `lean_leansearch "measure preserving translation of Lebesgue measure integral over translated ball"` -> `MeasureTheory.lintegral_add_right_eq_self`, `MeasureTheory.MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage` (`Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.LIntegral`, `.../Integral/Lebesgue/Map`). RESULT / CORRECTION: `Causalean.Mathlib.Analysis.HalfDiscPolar` is recorded here as an ANALOGOUS source only, NOT as reuse. Verified by reading the file: every declaration is stated on the origin-centred (or additively translated) upper half-disc `{z | 0 < z.2 ∧ planarRadius z ≤ r}` with a radial-times-angular SEPARABLE integrand (`halfDisc_weighted_polar_integral`, `halfDisc_radial_integral`) or is a cosine-cancellation corollary; there is no annulus/tube domain, no signed-normal-plus-arclength coordinate, and no nonseparable integrand such as \(\min\{1,(d(z,x_\star)/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\). It therefore cannot realize the circular-tube normalizer (1), the two-sided tube ball masses (3), or the translated local-ball bounds (5)-(6); it is the reference for the polar-factorization PROOF PATTERN (reduce a planar set integral to `polarCoord` + Tonelli), with the gap being annulus-vs-half-disc domain and translated-centre-vs-origin balls. Consequently the following LOCAL work is planned in `Helpers/TubeCoords.lean` (build-inline, small/medium, no Defer): (i) `tubePolarChart` — the tube parametrisation \(z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi)\) on \(|s|\le h_0<1\) with its area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\), obtained from Mathlib `polarCoord` + `integral_comp_polarCoord_symm`; (ii) `tubeJacobian_two_sided_bounds` — the uniform \(1-h_0\le 1+s\le 1+h_0\) Jacobian sandwich and the metric comparison \(c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\) of the core's equation (2), by compactness of \(S^1\); (iii) `translatedBall_sideMass_bounds` — the side-specific translated-ball mass comparisons (5)-(6) for a centre \(x\ne x_\star\), from (ii) plus translation invariance (`lintegral_add_right_eq_self`) and monotonicity of ball mass. Also still ANALOGOUS-only: the ANGULAR-GRID design on a square in `CausalSmith.Stat.BddUniformLogPenalty` (`packingSquare`, `angularPacking_geometry`, `angularDesignMeasure_map_distance_eq`, `packingBump`, `bernoulliGaussianLaw`) — different frontier geometry, positive design density, Bernoulli-Gaussian marks; it is the reference for the arc-packing / disjoint-cell counting behind \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\) and for the localized-perturbation KL localization. GENUINE reuse inside this block, unchanged: `Causalean.Mathlib.InformationTheory.gaussianKL_eq` (equal-variance Gaussian KL \((m_0-m_1)^2/(2v)\), used verbatim at equation (8)).
\(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

review.note: Equality with the finite product of P.observedLaw is equivalent to the sample law consisting of n independent draws from the observed law induced by P.

nl.statement: For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

review.note: The existential real constants are fixed across all 0 < h ≤ h₀, their stated ordering makes both positive and finite, and Mathlib's packingNumber is exactly the maximal cardinality of an h-separated subset.

nl.statement: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).

review.note: The two separate near-boundary inequalities are equivalent to the paper's maximum-of-two-infima condition, and the Fin 2 and side-support quantifiers match.

standard.citation: Gaïffas, S. (2005). Convergence Rates for Pointwise Curve Estimation with a Degenerate Design. Mathematical Methods of Statistics 14, 1--27; arXiv:math/0410354.

review.note: The bound matches exactly, while the Tendsto conjunct realizes the frozen global definition θₜ,P(x)=lim_{z→x,z∈Xₜ,P}gₜ,P(z), rather than adding an independent assumption.

standard.citation: Gaïffas, S. (2005). Convergence Rates for Pointwise Curve Estimation with a Degenerate Design. Mathematical Methods of Statistics 14, 1--27; arXiv:math/0410354.

nl.statement: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the one-sided restricted score measure \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\) on Borel sets \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^2\); there exists a single regular conditional law \(\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\) of the observed \(Y\) given \(X=z\) and, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), a \(\mu_{t,P}\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\subseteq\mathcal X_{t,P}\) such that, simultaneously for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\) and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}\exp\{\lambda(y-g_{t,P}(z))\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\le\exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.

review.note: Lean gives one Markov conditional kernel, one restricted-score null set per side, residual integrability, centering, and the same all-real sub-Gaussian MGF bound; N⊆sideSupport is existentially recoverable by intersection, and the extra integral-of-y identity follows from centering and integrability under the probability kernel.

standard.name: centered observed-side conditional sub-Gaussian regression noise; independent-error precedent only, with the restricted-kernel formulation derived here
standard.citation: Haris, A., A. Shojaie, and N. Simon (2019). Nonparametric Regression with Adaptive Truncation via a Convex Hierarchical Penalty. Biometrika 106(1), 87--107; doi:10.1093/biomet/asy056; arXiv:1611.09972.

nl.statement: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

review.note: On the stated domains cm > 0, κ > 2, and h > 0, ENNReal.ofReal faithfully embeds cm*h^κ, and localMass is exactly the paper's one-sided boundary-ball probability.

nl.statement: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).

For the stated positive parameters and h, ENNReal.ofReal embeds Cm*h^κ exactly, and 1 ≤ thinProfile is precisely the claimed nonempty thin-site packing condition.
For positive h, ENNReal.ofReal (cJ / h) is exactly the nonnegative embedding of c_J h⁻¹, and the existential positive cJ realizes the paper's fixed positive constant uniformly over every 0<h≤h0.

review.note: The local-mass inequality has exactly the paper's x, t, and h domains; Monotone m makes explicit the frozen symbol declaration that m is a nondecreasing modulus, with its total-domain representation conservatively restricting to (0,h0].

The structure is exactly the conjunction of the seven listed assumptions, with AdmissibleBaseParameters restating the declared domains L>0, σ>0, cₘ>0, κ>2, and 0<h₀<1.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

On the S1 domain 0 < c_m < C_m, the structure is equivalent to base-class membership conjoined with the isolated upper-profile and thin-site assumptions.
On the S1 domain 0 < c_m < C_m, the structure is equivalent to base-class membership conjoined with the pervasive-thin-sites assumption.
For the intrinsic domain n ≥ 1 and 0 < h₀ < 1, Finset.range through the natural ceiling represents exactly the stated dyadic grid.

Fin 2 has exactly the indices 0 and 1, so min (localMass P 0 x h) (localMass P 1 x h) is exactly min over t∈{0,1} of q_{t,P}(x,h) on the stated boundary and bandwidth domain. | Unfolding localMass gives exactly minₜ q_{t,P}(x,h): Fin 2 consists of 0 and 1, and on x ∈ 𝓑 and 0 < h ≤ h₀ the probability-valued result lies in [0,1]; Lean's values outside that domain are a conservative totalization of the same formula.

The boundary subtype enforces x∈𝓑, the nested infima equal the infimum over the dyadic grid, and the zero-mass guard gives the extended-real interpretation of inverse zero. | On the stated domains, the ENNReal infimum over the dyadic-grid membership proofs is exactly the paper infimum; the zero-mass guard faithfully realizes q_t⁻¹ = ∞, while nonzero probability masses and finite compact-boundary packing multiplicity make the toReal/getD expression equal to the displayed bias-stochastic term.

nl.statement: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).

The real inverse of max(Nₜ,n(x,h),1) multiplied by the conditional outcome sum is exactly the guarded local-constant fit, including value zero for an empty side ball.
Filtering the dyadic grid by 8 log(e+n/h)≤Nₜ,n(x,h) is equivalent to the paper's Nₜ,n(x,h)≥8 log(e+n h⁻¹).

nl.statement: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

review.note: For the finite nonempty admissible set, the minimizer set is finite and nonempty, so its sInf is exactly the numerically smallest criterion minimizer; the empty branch returns h0.

nl.statement: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

review.note: After unfolding the side fits and adaptive bandwidths, Lean defines exactly the treated adaptive fit minus the control adaptive fit.

nl.statement: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

review.note: On the stated nonempty shared-geometry domain, the nested infimum/suprema encode exactly the infimum over pointwise sample-measurable estimators of the worst-law expected boundary-supremum loss.

nl.statement: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

review.note: The predicate pins the circular regions, normalized score densities, independent Gaussian potential outcomes, and zero regressions/traces on their paper domains; the explicit observed-law equalities follow from the latent law, sharp assignment, and a.e. consistency. | Unfolding all referenced definitions gives the stated circular regions and normalized tube densities; their frontiers yield the unit circle, the product latent law is exactly independent N(0,σ²) potential outcomes independent of X, and the regression and trace fields vanish on their paper domains.

nl.statement: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

nl.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.

review.note: After unfolding the base class and localization laws, the five conjuncts exactly encode Lipschitz-representative uniqueness, support and trace identification, observed-law invariance, the normalized positive/zero-mass Y(t) compatibility, and its sharp-partition specialization; the final observed-kernel clause is already entailed by the base-class Gaussian-kernel assumption.

nl.statement: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

nl.statement: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

review.note: The fixed cm,Cm precede κ, the exact circular witness densities derive the stated uniform mass and packing comparisons, the class bundles include the isolated upper profile, and the zero regression/trace clauses match their natural domains.

nl.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).

nl.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.

nl.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \asymp (\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]

review.note: After unfolding the referenced definitions, the geometry-restricted iSup/lintegral terms are exactly the stated base-class expected loss and fallback probability; the κ-independent estimator and uniform c, C, N encode the displayed bounds, while pervasive-class inclusion gives the minimax sandwich and the empty-class definition R_n = ⊤ recovers the unconditional lower bound outside the stated nonempty asymptotic regime.

nl.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.

review.note: After unfolding exponentialModulus and AdmissibleSeverityExponent, h ≤ h0 is the modulus's intrinsic domain, the eventual positive-constant sandwich is exactly the stated asymptotic order, and that sandwich yields a positive decreasing h_n → 0 with n m_α(h_n)/log n → ∞; conversely the paper's clauses directly imply Lean's formulation.

nl.statement: For a declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), does there exist a data-measurable band \(\mathcal C_n\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma-o(1)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=O(1)\)? Prove the matching honest-width lower bound: every band sequence satisfying the displayed coverage condition obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\ge c\) for a universal \(c>0\). If the upper target is impossible, characterize exactly which pairs \((\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) and \((\kappa',\mathsf J'_{-},\mathsf J'_{+})\) in \(\Lambda_n\), separated by their \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) benchmark functions, must satisfy uniform score-law distinguishability \(\inf_{P,P'}\operatorname{TV}(P_X^{\otimes n},(P'_X)^{\otimes n})\to1\), where \(P\) and \(P'\) range over the corresponding two profile-restricted component classes.

nl.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.

review.note: The existential positive constant is uniform over M, laws, parameters, and estimators; the finite-KL clauses follow from either stated KL budget, measurability is intrinsic to expectation, and product experiments are instances of the generic law statement.

nl.statement:
Let \(M\ge2\), let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws on a common measurable space, and suppose \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)<\infty\) for every \(j\). For every decoder \(\widehat J\) taking values in \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\),
\[
 \frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\{\widehat J\ne j\}
 \ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)-\log2}{\log M}.
\]

nl.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

review.note: After unfolding the disk-pattern, dyadic-grid, conditional-product, score-product, and normalized-maximum definitions, Lean gives the same trace count, zero-empty-family convention, score-a.e. conditional tail bound, residual normalization, and expectation bound. | After unfolding the helper definitions, diskPatterns is exactly the nonempty side-specific boundary-disk trace family, scoreSampleLaw is P_X^⊗n, conditionalOutcomeProduct is the conditionally independent product of the single observed Y|X kernel supplied by CenteredSubGaussianKernel, and normalizedDiskResidualMax implements the stipulated zero-on-empty normalized residual maximum; the cardinality, tail, and conditional-expectation bounds agree in both directions.

nl.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), define \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\), and let \(\mathsf R_P\) and \(N_{t,P}\) be the conditional outcome kernel and side-specific null sets furnished by that assumption. For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\); in particular, all these conclusions hold \(\mu_{t,P}\)-almost everywhere on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\).

review.note: Unfolding CenteredSubGaussianKernel, restrictedScore, sideSupport, and scoreOutcomeLaw yields the same single conditional kernel, side-null sets, integrability, centering, MGF inequality, conditional regression mean, absolute-moment bound, and restricted-score a.e. scope. | After unfolding the named definitions, restrictedScore is the stated side-restricted score measure, and the Lean kernel, null-set, integrability, centering, MGF, absolute-moment, conditional-mean, and almost-everywhere content is equivalent to the paper claim; intersecting N with sideSupport supplies the paper's harmless N⊆𝒳 normalization.

nl.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

review.note: After unfolding the class, risk, grid, benchmark, feasible-radius, estimator, and rate definitions, Lean and the frozen statement agree in both directions; eventual grid membership is the faithful asymptotic reading, and nonemptiness plus modulus monotonicity permits a decreasing bandwidth representative.

nl.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ's lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.

review.note: After unfolding the class, geometry, risk, rate, witness-certificate, and iid definitions, Lean states the same circular-class inclusion, eventual two-sided pervasive-rate bound, exact eventual rate ratio, and divergence; the geometry and certificate premises make explicit the paper's circular setup and certified uniform constants.

nl.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), fix an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\), and suppose \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\). For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), and every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
\]
there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the first conclusion, and it obeys the second conclusion whenever widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. These conclusions hold for every such assignment geometry; the circular laws are needed only as explicit nonemptiness witnesses.

review.note: All nonemptiness, honesty, and width suprema use the same geometry-restricted classes; a nonempty restricted pervasive class supplies global boundary entropy on B, and the large-n pervasive and base-transfer conclusions match both displayed bounds. | After unfolding the geometry-restricted law classes, coverage, half-width, rates, and local benchmark, Lean states the same pervasive-class honesty hypothesis, two eventual lower bounds, and base-class transfer; the fixed-geometry equalities identify every law's boundary with B, and base honesty entails pervasive honesty.

nl.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\). For any admissible assignment geometry under the preceding premises, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), for every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and every sequence \(\epsilon_n\downarrow0\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n
\]
obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 \frac{\mathbb E_PW_n(x)}{r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)}
 \ge c_\gamma.
\]
Every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the global lower bound because \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\), and it obeys the ratio conclusion when widths are compared over its pervasive subclass. The circular witnesses in \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) certify explicit nonemptiness only. Thus, whenever the pervasive class is nonempty, the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive and base classes.

Independently of the preceding pervasive-class conclusions, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Uniform local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union, the corresponding local-ratio converse for unions without a nonempty pervasive component, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion stated only through score-law total variation remain open. The global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can remain bounded at an isolated thin site, and score-law total variation alone does not control the distance between full observed laws.
